settings_save_on_committed.instructions: Does ANY added or modified production call site in the Git diff violate the onCommitted rule for settings persistence? Unit test files (such as *.test.ts or *.spec.ts) that invoke the helpers only to assert callback behavior are explicitly out of scope and must NOT be flagged as violations. Specifically, in production code (non-test .ts and .svelte files): does the diff add or modify any call to saveToggleSetting, saveStringSetting, saveOptionalRangeSetting, or saveSettingBatch (or a direct setSetting call in settings) where savedSnapshot is updated only after awaiting the helper's boolean return value instead of inside the onCommitted callback, OR where the onCommitted callback is a no-op (such as () => {}) or omits updating the corresponding savedSnapshot field? Answer Yes if even a single production call site in the diff violates this, even when other hunks in the same file are compliant.

criteria.true_description: At least one added or modified production (non-test) settings save call in the diff passes an empty/no-op onCommitted callback (e.g. () => {}) or updates savedSnapshot outside onCommitted (such as inside an if (await save*Setting(...)) branch).
criteria.false_description: Every added or modified production settings save call in the diff updates the corresponding savedSnapshot field inside its onCommitted callback immediately after DB write succeeds, or the diff only touches unit test files (*.test.ts / *.spec.ts) or does not modify production settings save call sites.

rust_no_module_cycle_and_hook_wiring.instructions: Does ANY added or modified non-test Rust code in the Git diff violate the 3-layer module dependency rule for src-tauri/src/? Specifically, answer Yes if the diff introduces ANY of: (1) a reverse reference from a lower shared module (db, model, or util) to any domain module or upper layer module (lib, main, commands, error), OR (2) a reverse reference from a domain module (such as mpv, chat, feed, livewait, metaresolve, innertube, filter, sponsor, yt, ui, deep_link, deps, diag, or native_host) to an upper layer module (lib, main, commands, or error, e.g. crate::error::UiError or crate::commands::*), OR (3) a direct cross-domain reference that creates a circular/mutual dependency of 2 or more modules (for example mpv directly importing or calling crate::chat::* when chat already depends on mpv) instead of injecting a hook/callback or trait from lib.rs or commands. Acyclic one-way references between domain modules (e.g. chat -> innertube or chat -> filter without a reverse edge) and test-only code (#[cfg(test)], #[cfg(all(test, ...))], tests/*) are ALLOWED and must NOT be flagged.

criteria.true_description: The diff adds or modifies non-test Rust code under src-tauri/src/ that introduces: a reverse reference from db/model/util to a domain or upper layer module, a reverse reference from a domain module to an upper layer module (lib/main/commands/error), or a direct peer-module reference that forms a circular dependency (such as mpv importing crate::chat::* while chat depends on mpv) instead of using a hook/callback injected from lib.rs or commands.
criteria.false_description: All added or modified non-test Rust imports and calls respect the 3-layer direction (upper lib/main/commands/error -> domain -> shared db/model/util), contain no reverse references to upper layers or from shared to domain, and contain only acyclic one-way domain references or hook/callback wiring from lib.rs/commands; or the diff only touches test code or does not modify src-tauri/src/**/*.rs.

library_async_mutation_and_cursor_guards.instructions: Does ANY added or modified non-test code in the Git diff for async playlist operations violate the library async mutation, mutual exclusion, or paging cursor guards? Unit test files (such as *.test.ts or *.spec.ts) and test-only code are explicitly out of scope and must NOT be flagged. Specifically, in non-test files under src/lib/library-page*.ts or src/lib/Library*.svelte, answer Yes if the diff introduces ANY of: (1) an omitted or weakened operation guard: in refreshPlaylists(), omitting listRun / listAgain serialization coalescing concurrent requests, awaiting listReorderRun, listsReq stale-response discard (req === listsReq), OR ++listsSnapshotSeq on snapshot update; in sync (syncPlaylist), omitting either playlistMutSeq or listsSnapshotSeq capture/comparison OR omitting refreshPlaylists() on conflict/snapshot mismatch; in delayed Undo restore, omitting listsSnapshotSeq comparison, ++listsReq, bumpPlaylistMut, OR refreshPlaylists() when listsSnapshotSeq changed during restore (note: restore does NOT require playlistMutSeq comparison); in remove (removeItem) after playlist_remove succeeds, omitting ++listsReq OR bumpPlaylistMut(playlistId); in create, delete, rename, or import, omitting ++listsReq, bumpPlaylistMut, or refreshPlaylists() where applicable; in list reorder (applyListOrder / persistListOrder), omitting ++listsReq, listReorderRun serialization, OR refreshPlaylists() on failure; in item reorder (persistOrder), omitting reorderRun serialization, ++itemsReq, OR playlist_items refetch on failure; in bulk ops (runBulkOp), omitting sortBusy + await reorderRun serialization, ++itemsReq, OR playlist_items refetch on completion (note: runBulkOp does NOT require playlist_items refetch on failure); OR in loadMore (loadMoreItems), omitting its itemsReq / selectedId stale-response guard (note: loadMore intentionally does NOT call refreshPlaylists() or use playlistMutSeq / listsSnapshotSeq and must NOT be flagged for omitting them); (2) a single ad-hoc boolean flag instead of the existing mutual exclusion state (syncingId / plLoadingMore / removingIds / restoringIds / sortBusy / restoring) paired with matching UI disabled states in src/lib/Library*.svelte; or (3) an update to plTailPos or plHasMore that drops plTailDirty tracking, or a playlist create, delete, or select path that omits resetting cursor / hasMore / plTailDirty. Answer Yes if even a single non-test hunk violates any of (1), (2), or (3).

criteria.true_description: At least one added or modified non-test hunk under src/lib/library-page*.ts or src/lib/Library*.svelte either: (1) omits listRun / listAgain serialization coalescing concurrent requests, awaiting listReorderRun, listsReq stale-response discard (req === listsReq), OR ++listsSnapshotSeq on snapshot update inside refreshPlaylists(); omits playlistMutSeq OR listsSnapshotSeq capture/comparison OR refreshPlaylists() on conflict/snapshot mismatch in sync (syncPlaylist); omits listsSnapshotSeq comparison, ++listsReq, bumpPlaylistMut, OR refreshPlaylists() on snapshot change in delayed Undo restore; omits ++listsReq OR bumpPlaylistMut(playlistId) after playlist_remove succeeds in removeItem; omits ++listsReq, bumpPlaylistMut, or refreshPlaylists() where applicable in create, delete, rename, or import; omits ++listsReq, listReorderRun, OR refreshPlaylists() on failure in applyListOrder / persistListOrder; omits reorderRun serialization, ++itemsReq, OR playlist_items refetch on failure in persistOrder; omits sortBusy + await reorderRun, ++itemsReq, OR playlist_items refetch on completion in runBulkOp; OR omits the itemsReq / selectedId stale-response guard in loadMore (loadMoreItems); (2) uses a single ad-hoc boolean instead of mutual exclusion (syncingId / plLoadingMore / removingIds / restoringIds / sortBusy / restoring) paired with matching UI disabled states in src/lib/Library*.svelte; or (3) updates plTailPos / plHasMore while dropping plTailDirty tracking or omits resetting cursor / hasMore / plTailDirty on playlist create, delete, or select.
criteria.false_description: All added or modified non-test async playlist operations preserve their applicable guards: refreshPlaylists() preserves listRun / listAgain serialization coalescing concurrent requests, awaits listReorderRun, enforces listsReq stale-response discard (req === listsReq), and increments ++listsSnapshotSeq on snapshot update; sync (syncPlaylist) captures and compares both playlistMutSeq and listsSnapshotSeq and calls refreshPlaylists() on conflict/snapshot mismatch; delayed Undo restore compares listsSnapshotSeq, increments listsReq, calls bumpPlaylistMut, and calls refreshPlaylists() when listsSnapshotSeq changed during restore (without requiring playlistMutSeq comparison); removeItem increments listsReq and calls bumpPlaylistMut(playlistId) after playlist_remove succeeds; create, delete, rename, and import preserve ++listsReq, bumpPlaylistMut, and refreshPlaylists() where applicable; list reorder (applyListOrder / persistListOrder) preserves ++listsReq, listReorderRun, and refreshPlaylists() on failure; item reorder (persistOrder) preserves reorderRun serialization, ++itemsReq, and playlist_items refetch on failure; bulk ops (runBulkOp) preserve sortBusy + await reorderRun, ++itemsReq, and playlist_items refetch on completion (without requiring playlist_items refetch on failure); loadMore (loadMoreItems) preserves its itemsReq / selectedId stale-response guard (without requiring refreshPlaylists() or playlistMutSeq / listsSnapshotSeq); mutual exclusion (syncingId / plLoadingMore / removingIds / restoringIds / sortBusy / restoring) is paired with matching UI disabled states in src/lib/Library*.svelte; and plTailDirty tracking plus cursor / hasMore / plTailDirty reset on create / delete / select are preserved; or the diff only touches unit test files (*.test.ts / *.spec.ts) or does not modify src/lib/library-page*.ts or src/lib/Library*.svelte.

rust_db_import_epoch_toctou.instructions: Does ANY added or modified non-test Rust write path in the Git diff release Db::lock() across an .await or a deferred Undo snapshot and then write to SQLite by integer row ID (e.g. playlist.id) without capturing Db::import_epoch before lock release and re-verifying it inside the final write transaction? Test-only code (#[cfg(test)], #[cfg(all(test, ...))], tests/*) and single unbroken DB-lock writes (that do not release Db::lock() across .await or a deferred Undo snapshot) are explicitly out of scope and must NOT be flagged. Specifically, in non-test code under src-tauri/src/db/**/*.rs or src-tauri/src/commands/**/*.rs, answer Yes if a write path releases Db::lock() across .await or a deferred Undo snapshot and performs an integer-row-ID SQLite write without: (1) reading Db::import_epoch before releasing the lock, AND (2) re-verifying import_epoch equality inside the final write transaction and aborting with DbError::StaleSync (or equivalent) on mismatch.

criteria.true_description: At least one added or modified non-test Rust write path under src-tauri/src/db/**/*.rs or src-tauri/src/commands/**/*.rs releases Db::lock() across an .await or a deferred Undo snapshot and then writes to SQLite by integer row ID (e.g. playlist.id) without capturing Db::import_epoch before lock release and re-verifying import_epoch inside the final write transaction (aborting with DbError::StaleSync or equivalent on mismatch).
criteria.false_description: Every added or modified non-test Rust write path that releases Db::lock() across an .await or a deferred Undo snapshot before writing to SQLite by integer row ID captures Db::import_epoch before lock release and re-verifies equality inside the final write transaction (aborting with DbError::StaleSync or equivalent on mismatch); or the diff only modifies single unbroken DB-lock writes, test-only code (#[cfg(test)] / tests/*), or files outside src-tauri/src/db/**/*.rs and src-tauri/src/commands/**/*.rs.
